references.text: Jesus calls Simon "Simon, son of Jona" and gives him the name Peter (Greek: Petros, Aramaic: Kefas), which means "rock". This corresponds to [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42] where Jesus already at their first meeting gives Simon this new name. Note that the patronym is different: Matthew writes "Barjona", while John writes "son of John".
In [ref:Mark 3:16|Mark 3:16], Jesus gives Simon the nickname Peter when he chooses the twelve apostles. This confirms the name change first announced in [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42].

In [ref:Luk 6:14|Luke 6:14], "Simon, whom he also called Peter" is mentioned in connection with the choosing of the apostles. This refers to the same name change Jesus announced in [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42].

In [ref:1 Mos 17:5|Genesis 17:5], God changes Abram's name to Abraham as a sign of his new calling and promise. Similarly, Jesus gives Simon a new name, Kefas/Peter, as a sign of his future role and identity.

In [ref:1 Mos 32:28|Genesis 32:28], God changes Jacob's name to Israel. The name change signals a new identity and a divine calling, just as Jesus naming Simon Kefas/Peter does in [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42].

In [ref:Joh 1:40-41|John 1:40-41], it is told that Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who followed Jesus, and that he then found his brother Simon and told him "We have found the Messiah". This leads directly to verse 42 where Andrew brings Simon to Jesus.

In [ref:1 Kor 1:12|1 Corinthians 1:12], the name Kefas (the Aramaic name Jesus gave Simon) is used. Paul refers to Simon Peter as Kefas, the same name that Jesus gave him according to [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42].

In [ref:Gal 2:9|Galatians 2:9], Paul mentions "James, Cephas and John" as pillars of the church. The name Kefas used here is the Aramaic name Jesus gave Simon in [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42], which the Gospel of John explains means Peter (rock).

In [ref:Jes 62:2|Isaiah 62:2], it is promised that God's people will be called by a new name that the Lord's mouth will set. The motif of God giving a new name has a parallel in Jesus' action in [ref:Joh 1:42|John 1:42], where he gives Simon the new name Kefas/Peter.
